cleanIntro: The BLK is a Turkish-made bolt-action rifle in .308 and 30-06 with a detachable box magazine and a two-position safety behind the bolt handle. It comes apart in a short, fixed order: magazine out, bolt out past the bolt stop on the left side, then — to clean the action — the two guard screws out and the stock lifted off the receiver and trigger assembly. The book asks for a cleaning after firing, before and after long storage, and whenever the rifle has been in rain, snow, salt water, dirt or mud.

steps.title: Safety pulled back to S
steps.action: The safety sits on the right side of the receiver, just behind the bolt handle. Pull it fully back toward the S mark. Forward toward F is FIRE.
steps.prose: Fingers outside the trigger guard while you work it. The book asks for S before any handling, loading or unloading — and S does not stop the bolt from opening, so the rest of the clearing is done on safe.
steps.quote: To activate the safety control, pull it fully back toward the “S” SAFE mark (See figure 1).
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — SAFETY MECHANISM, printed p.9

steps.title: Magazine latch pressed, magazine out
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction. Press the magazine latch in front of the trigger guard and take the magazine out of the bottom of the receiver.
steps.prose: A rifle with its magazine out can still have a round in the chamber. The chamber comes next, before anything else.
steps.quote: Depress the magazine latch in front of the trigger guard and remove the magazine from the bottom of the receiver.
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — UNLOADING, printed p.14
steps.warn: At this stage in the unloading process, the rifle may still have a live round in the chamber, which can be fired even though the box magazine has been removed.

steps.title: Bolt up and slowly back — chamber emptied
steps.action: Lift the bolt handle and draw the bolt slowly all the way to the rear so the extractor brings any round out of the chamber.
steps.prose: Slowly, so a live round comes out where you can catch it rather than across the bench. Count what comes out.
steps.quote: Lift the bolt handle and pull the bolt slowly to the rear to remove the cartridge from the chamber.
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — UNLOADING, printed p.14

steps.title: Look: chamber and magazine well empty
steps.action: With the bolt fully to the rear, look into the chamber and the magazine well and confirm there is nothing in either. Empty the magazine too, and keep the cartridges away from the bench.
steps.prose: A look, not an assumption. The book has you check the chamber and the magazine well a second time with the bolt still open before you go on.
steps.quote: With the bolt open (fully to the rear), look into the chamber and magazine well to ensure all cartridges have been removed.
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — UNLOADING, printed p.14

steps.title: Bolt fully back, bolt stop release pressed on the left
steps.action: Safety on S, finger off the trigger. With the bolt handle up and the bolt pulled completely to the rear, press the bolt stop release on the left side of the receiver.
steps.prose: The bolt stop is what holds the bolt in at the end of its travel. Hold the release in while you draw the bolt out in the next step.
steps.quote: Press the bolt stop release located on the left side (See Figure 5).
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — BOLT DISASSEMBLY, printed p.10
steps.warn: Never attempt to install or remove the bolt on a loaded firearm.

steps.title: Bolt slid out the back of the receiver
steps.action: Slide the bolt assembly straight out of the rear of the receiver.
steps.prose: Lay it on a clean cloth. With the bolt out the bore is open from the chamber end, which is how the book has you clean it.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt assembly by sliding it out of the rifle.
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — BOLT DISASSEMBLY, printed p.10

steps.title: Rifle upside down, stock screws out
steps.action: For cleaning the action: turn the rifle upside down and take out the stock screws through the trigger guard.
steps.prose: The parts list names two of them, a front and a rear guard screw. Keep them apart from each other so each goes back in its own hole.
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — CLEANING THE ACTION, printed p.15

steps.title: Stock lifted off the receiver and trigger assembly
steps.action: Lift the stock away from the receiver and the trigger assembly.
steps.prose: Lift it straight. The trigger assembly stays with the receiver — it is not taken apart, and the book allows no adjustment to it except the trigger pull weight.
steps.quote: Lift the stock off the receiver and trigger assembly.
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — CLEANING THE ACTION, printed p.15

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Magazine, bolt and stock are off the barrelled action. The book stops here.
steps.prose: Anything further goes to a qualified gunsmith or back to EAA, in the book's own words.
steps.quote: NEVER ATTEMPT TO DISASSEMBLE YOUR RIFLE BEYOND THE INSTRUCTIONS PROVIDED IN THIS MANUAL.
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — CLEANING FREQUENCY, printed p.16

steps.title: Solvent-soaked brush through the full length of the bore
steps.action: Fit a rod and brush of the right caliber, soak the brush in gun cleaning solvent or bore cleaner, and push it through the entire length of the barrel several times.
steps.prose: The bolt is out, so work from the chamber end. Let the solvent sit on the fouling for a minute before the patches.
steps.quote: Push the cleaning rod and brush through the entire length of the barrel several times.
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — CLEANING THE BARREL, printed p.15

steps.title: Dry patches until one comes out clean
steps.action: Take the brush off, fit a dry patch to the patch holder, and push it through several times. Keep changing patches until they come out clean.
steps.prose: A dirty patch means there is still fouling in the bore. Clean patches are the stopping point, not a count.
steps.quote: Push the rod and dry patch through the barrel several times. Repeat with clean patches until they come out clean.
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — CLEANING THE BARREL, printed p.15

steps.title: Oiled patch, then a dry patch to take the excess out
steps.action: Push a patch soaked in gun oil through the barrel several times, then a dry patch several times to remove the excess oil. Look through the bore and make sure no patch is left inside.
steps.prose: The dry patch is the point. The book wants a dry, clean bore and chamber before the rifle is fired again — oil left in the bore is an obstruction.
steps.quote: Push the dry patch through the barrel several times to remove any excess oil.
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — CLEANING THE BARREL, printed p.15

steps.title: Bolt and receiver wiped clean of powder residue
steps.action: With a patch or a soft clean cloth, wipe powder residue and anything else off the bolt and the receiver surfaces. For congealed lubricant or hard deposits, use a quality action cleaner.
steps.prose: The stock is off, so the whole receiver is in reach. Leave the trigger assembly alone beyond wiping it.
steps.quote: Use a patch or a soft, clean cloth to remove powder residue and any other foreign material from the bolt and receiver surfaces.
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — CLEANING THE ACTION, printed p.15

steps.title: A light film of oil on the bolt and receiver — no more
steps.action: Apply a light film of quality gun oil along the bolt and the receiver surfaces.
steps.prose: A light film is all the book asks for. Too much oil collects dirt and, by the book's own warning, can affect safe operation.
steps.quote: Apply a light film of quality gun oil along the bolt and receiver surfaces.
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — CLEANING THE ACTION, printed p.15
steps.warn: Do not use lubricants that thicken or congeal.

steps.title: Outside of the barrel oiled with a soft cloth
steps.action: Wipe a thin coat of gun oil onto the outside of the barrel with a soft, clean cloth, and wipe down the other external metal.
steps.prose: A thin coat keeps rust off. Before the rifle is used again, wipe off the excess.
steps.quote: Apply a thin coat of gun oil to the outside of the barrel using a soft, clean cloth.
steps.cite: Blk Bolt Action Rifle — OWNER'S MANUAL (European American Armory Corporation) — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — CLEANING THE BARREL, printed p.15

deepAbsentReason: The BLK book's disassembly ends with the bolt out (printed p.10) and, to clean the action, the stock screws out and the stock lifted off the receiver and trigger assembly (printed p.15). It then warns never to disassemble the rifle beyond the instructions in the manual and sends further cleaning, service or repair to a qualified gunsmith or back to EAA (printed p.16). The trigger-pull adjustment it describes (printed pp.11-12) is an adjustment, not a disassembly. Nothing deeper is published, so nothing deeper is walked.

cleaning.name: BARREL & BORE
tasks: Rod and brush of the right caliber, brush soaked in solvent or bore cleaner
Brush pushed through the entire length of the barrel several times
Dry patches until they come out clean
Oiled patch through several times, then a dry patch to remove the excess
Bore looked through: no patch or obstruction left inside
⛔ Never fire with oil, grease or any obstruction in the bore or chamber

cleaning.name: BOLT & RECEIVER
tasks: Powder residue wiped off the bolt and receiver with a patch or soft cloth
Action cleaner for congealed lubricant or hard deposits
A light film of gun oil along the bolt and receiver
Do not use lubricants that thicken or congeal
Do not adjust anything on the trigger assembly except the pull weight

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & STORAGE
tasks: Thin coat of gun oil on the outside of the barrel with a soft cloth
External metal wiped with oil from time to time against rust
Excess oil removed, chamber and bore dried, before the next use
After salt water: rinse in fresh water, dry, clean and oil

reassembly: No ammunition on the bench. Safety on S.
Trigger guard assembly onto the stock, then the stock over the receiver and trigger assembly.
Front and rear guard (stock) screws back in and tightened.
Empty magazine back into the magazine well until the latch holds it.
Before the bolt: look through the barrel and confirm it is completely free of obstructions.
Bolt: line up the bolt lugs with the receiver, slide the bolt in and push it fully forward.
To close the bolt, press the handle down. The safety must be off (F, red indicator showing) for the bolt to close — put it back on S as soon as the bolt is down.
Function check before any live ammunition.
fncheck: From the book, after cleaning (printed p.15): confirm the chamber and magazine are empty, muzzle in a safe direction. Move the safety to F and close the bolt firmly — the firing pin must stay cocked. Pull the trigger — the firing pin must release. Do this at least ten times. If the firing pin does not stay cocked when the bolt is closed firmly, the book says to return the rifle to the factory or have a qualified gunsmith inspect it. Finish with the safety back on S.
